item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO -- Through Nick Pivetta’s first four starts this season, it was clear he was picking up right where he left off from his career-best 2025 campaign, one that saw him finish sixth in National League Cy Young Award voting … only for it to be derailed by a right elbow injury in April that cost him nearly five months.
But upon his return on Sept. 7, Pivetta reassumed the version of himself that was prevalent throughout last year, putting a lengthy rehab behind him and leaving no doubt that he was fully ready to contribute on the biggest stage.
This time, though, he’ll have the Petco Park crowd behind him.
“We're very lucky to have such a great fan base here,” Pivetta said. “From what I've heard from the guys that have played here before, I'm expecting great things and very excited for it. Just trying to keep all my focus on the game, but enjoy those moments, too, with those fans and try to bring the championship home for them.”
Since returning from the injured list, Pivetta has looked a lot like the guy who posted a 2.87 ERA across 31 starts in ‘25. He allowed a mere three runs over 18 2/3 innings over four starts, good for a 1.45 ERA. He delivered 4 2/3 scoreless frames against the Dodgers in Los Angeles his last time out, helping the Padres secure their third consecutive trip to the postseason that night.
“High level of confidence with Nick, what a road he’s been on this year,” Padres manager Craig Stammen said. “For him, when it didn’t look great at the beginning of the season, to put in the work over an entire season and not know if he’s ever going to get back … now he’s [been] one of our best pitchers down the stretch.”
The four-start runway Pivetta had allowed him to build up to full pitch count (he threw 87 pitches in his last start), meaning there should be zero limitations for him this postseason.
Of course, the Padres almost certainly won’t need him to go a full four or five innings, given their elite bullpen that was pieced together specifically to help shorten games in the playoffs -- a formula that San Diego has deployed with great success in its previous seasons and seems poised to do once more.
But Pivetta’s postseason track record is nothing to scoff at.
He was brilliant for the Red Sox during their playoff run in 2021 that saw him come out of the bullpen in the American League Division Series against the Rays before he twirled five innings of one-run ball against the eventual World Series champion Astros in Game 4 of the AL Championship Series. And, of course, he held the Cubs to just two runs over five innings and struck out nine in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series last year, capping off an excellent first season in San Diego.
That Chicago lineup will be a little different this time -- much stronger, for one. He’ll have to navigate a top of the order that includes the likely NL MVP in center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and a surging Alex Bregman, who posted a 1.010 OPS in the second half.
“It's a whole lineup; they make good contact, they don't swing outside of the zone,” Pivetta said. “They have guys in there that jell really well together, led by Bregman. It's just trying to keep them off-balance, but always sticking to my strengths and doing what I do best and just see where that night goes.”
Pivetta is up for the challenge.
“I'm healthy, I'm feeling good and I'm excited for the next step,” he said.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have yet to begin their quest for a three-peat during these MLB playoffs, which are already underway, but on paper, LA is going to be a tough out regardless of its opponent.
However, even though the MLB playoffs are underway, it’s not too early to start thinking about the major offseason decision the team faces regarding ace starter Tarik Skubal.
Recently, in an MLB free agent predictions piece, Tarik Skubal is being linked back to the Los Angeles Dodgers on a 10-year deal.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce 3 Sudden Roster Moves Amid MLB Playoffs
Dodgers Predicted to Retain Tarik Skubal
Back in August, the Dodgers shocked the MLB world by landing Tarik Skubal in a huge trade with the Detroit Tigers.
However, they (LA) face a big decision regarding his free-agent status, as he is set to hit the open market after the 2026 season.
BleacherReport.com’s Zach Buckley recently predicted LA to retain its new ace via a 10-year deal:
“Prediction: Skubal re-signs with the Dodgers on a 10-year deal.”
“In short, the crystal ball sees this coming down to the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets—two of the biggest spenders in baseball. The Dodgers just made an aggressive move for Skubal at this year’s trade deadline, while the Mets badly need a boost to their rotation. This bidding war should be ferocious, but in the end, the Dodgers’ head start by having Skubal already on the roster could be what pushes them over the edge.”
More MLB on Heavy: MLB World Reacts to Austin Riley Moment in Phillies-Braves Game
Tarik Skubal Has Proved His Worth with Los Angeles
Let’s be clear: the 2X AL Cy Young winner in Tarik Skubal, doesn’t have to prove his worth to anybody, but since joining the Dodgers, he’s made it really hard for the team to ignore that he would be an immense addition to the starting rotation.
Across 10 starts with LA, Skubal holds a 2.61 ERA with 70 strikeouts.
He will be a huge piece to the Dodgers postseason fold, and if he really helps propel LA to a three-peat, that might be enough to truly force Andrew Friedman’s hand in his ongoing contract talks.
Dodgers fans, do you want to bring back Tarik Skubal? And at what price would you be willing to do so?

item.content:encoded:
The Philadelphia Phillies traded for Luis Arraez to make their lineup deeper when they reached the MLB playoffs.
But now in the postseason, and facing elimination on Wednesday against the Atlanta Braves, the Phillies don’t even have Arraez available to play for them.
It’s an unfortunate reality, and it’s one the Phillies are going to have to navigate if they want to see Arraez put on their uniform again.
The Phillies lost the NL Wild Card Series opener on Tuesday to the Braves when Austin Riley hit a go-ahead home run for Atlanta in the eighth inning.
In a best-of-three series, it’s Wednesday or bust for the Phillies.
Arraez will only be able to watch and hope he gets another chance before Philadelphia’s season is over.
And given that Arraez’s contract expires after this season, he may never play for the Phillies again if they lose on Wednesday.
When is Luis Arraez Coming Back?
There’s no real clarity on Arraez’s return timeline yet.
The veteran sprained his left ankle on Thursday, Sept. 24, while running on the bases. He went down in a lot of pain and had to essentially be carried off the field.
The Phillies left him off of the NL Wild Card Series roster. Otto Kemp, a utility player with a great old-school baseball name, is on the roster for this series in Arraez’s place.
“We still get improvement every day, but not enough,” Mattingly told reporters on Monday about Arraez. “He was going to try to hit today and just wasn’t able to do it. So, we kind of crossed that bridge today.”
Arraez hadn’t swung a bat yet as of the time Mattingly spoke to reporters on Monday.
The contact wizard was also seen with a boot on his foot during the Phillies’ celebrations on Sunday after they clinched a playoff spot.
Arraez won’t be eligible to play against the Braves in the Wild Card Series since he was left off the roster.
That means that he can only play if the Phillies win the best-of-three series in Atlanta.
At that point, the Phillies would get the chance to name a Divisional Series roster. Players can be swapped in and out then, which would allow Arraez back into the mix if he’s ready.
Luis Arraez Stats
Arraez has been solid since coming to Philadelphia. He’s batted .278 with 10 doubles, two home runs and 21 RBI in 46 games.
He had been hitting .324 with the Giants before the trade.
He’s also made major strides as a second base defensive player in 2026, going from a negative there to a clear positive — although a sprained ankle might not help.
Arraez had settled into the cleanup spot for the Phillies — a very new-age decision to put the best contact hitter on the team at the 4-spot in the batting order. It was mostly working, though, and Philadelphia has to win without Arraez to give him another chance to get back in the lineup.

item.content:encoded:
starting pitcher Kevin Gausman revealed his honest thoughts about the Toronto Blue Jays trading him at the MLB trade deadline.
Gausman, who starts for the Cubs on Wednesday against the San Diego Padres in a must-win game in the MLB Wild Card round, was dealt from Toronto to Chicago at the deadline for Brett Bateman and Ty Southisene.
According to the veteran hurler, the trade surprised him, as a conversation with Blue Jays GM Ross Atkins led him to believe he wasn't going to be dealt.
Kevin Gausman Shares Honest Thoughts on Blue Jays Trade
Speaking on the "Baseball Isn't Boring" podcast, Gausman shared his honest thoughts about the trade sending him from "The Six" to "The Windy City" at the deadline.
"We kind of had some conversations a couple days leading up that there was some interest. But (the Jays) didn't feel like it was going to get to a point where they thought they were going to get what they wanted to trade me," Gausman said (via Toronto Sun).
"They picked up a starter (Jameson Taillon) and (I thought), 'OK, probably going to lose a starter.' I didn't think it was going to be me, to be honest. But this game is crazy and you never know what's going to happen."
Cubs Need Kevin Gausman to Pitch Like An Ace in Playoffs
After dropping Game 1 of a possible three-game Wild Card series against San Diego by a score of 8-0, the Cubs are in a must-win situation on Wednesday when Gausman takes the mound against Nick Pivetta and the Padres.
With the Cubs following the trade, Gausman was 4-2 with a 4.83 ERA in nine starts for Chicago. He wasn't exactly what the team was hoping for, but if he can put up a great start for Chicago against San Diego and help the team force a deciding Game 3 in the Wild Card round, then it will make the trade look a lot better for the Cubs.
A free agent following this season, Gausman could potentially look to make a reunion in Toronto if he decides to pitch again.
He admitted on the podcast that being traded away from Toronto was so tough for him and his family as they all loved living and playing north of the border.
"I had been in Toronto for so long and so comfortable with the organization, it was my second home. We had a home. It was hard to leave, to be honest. A lot of great moments, not so great moments and (this) year was a really tough year to be a part of. The hardest part was the family aspect. My kids having to go to a new family room and trying to make friends in a short period of time. That was probably the hardest part, seeing how much it affected my wife and kids. They got comfortable just like I did," Gausman said.
We'll see what the future holds for Gausman, but right now, his focus is on winning Game 2 for the Cubs against the Padres.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] MLB Playoff Roundup: Austin Riley’s blast stuns Phillies
item.dc:creator: Matt Ferenchick
item.description: Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series couldn't have gone much better for the Yankees. On the mound, Cam Schlittler was excellent, blanking the Red Sox for 6.1 impressive innings. Then, led by Ben Rice, the Yankees' offense plated nine runs, pulling away from Boston to go up 1-0 in the series. Yesterday wasn't just the opening of the Yankees-Red Sox series, though. All three of the Wild Card matchups also got underway on Tuesday, so let's check in on what happened. AL Wild Card Series Game 1 Chicago
item.content:encoded:
Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series couldn't have gone much better for the Yankees. On the mound, Cam Schlittler was excellent, blanking the Red Sox for 6.1 impressive innings. Then, led by Ben Rice, the Yankees' offense plated nine runs, pulling away from Boston to go up 1-0 in the series.
Yesterday wasn't just the opening of the Yankees-Red Sox series, though. All three of the Wild Card matchups also got underway on Tuesday, so let's check in on what happened.
AL Wild Card Series Game 1
Chicago White Sox 6, Houston Astros 3
(Chicago leads 1-0)
After jumping out to a 3-0 lead early, the White Sox withstood the Astros and tacked on some more runs late to take the opener of the other AL matchup in Houston.
Facing an Astros' bullpen game, the White Sox got going quickly. With a runner on third in the first, Munetaka Murakami hit a fly ball that was deep enough for Chicago's Sam Antonacci to tag up and score. The next inning, Antonacci did it at the plate, hitting a bases loaded single to bring home two more runs. A Colson Montgomery homer in the fourth and a Chase Meidroth RBI single in the fifth had Chicago up big before Houston showed any resistance.
A two-run shot from Nelson Velázquez in the bottom of the fifth got the Astros on the board, but Chicago got one of those runs back a little while later. Houston countered with one in the eighth and brought the tying run to the plate, but couldn't cash in as the ChiSox held on from there. Amusingly, the Astros have now lost eight consecutive playoff games in Houston since early on in the 2023 playoffs. If Chicago can win one more at Daikin Park either today or tomorrow, they'll not only eliminate Houston but also secure their first playoff series victory since winning the 2005 World Series, over two decades ago. The Astros will have their best pitcher going for them in Hunter Brown, so we'll see if that's enough to keep their season alive.
NL Wild Card Series Game 1
Atlanta Braves 5, Philadelphia Phillies 3
(Atlanta leads 1-0)
Austin Riley's go-ahead eighth inning home run stunned the Phillies to give the Braves the series opener.
The Phillies opened the scoring early when Alec Bohm doubled home a run in the top of the first. Atlanta then answered back with Mike Yastrzemski RBI single. The game remained tied for a while after that as both Chris Sale and Jesús Luzardo put in solid outings; Luzardo hadn't necessarily been expected to even last five innings, as he was still relatively fresh off the IL and threw an inning of relief just to help the Phillies clinch a playof spot on Sunday. Things changed as both teams got to the bullpen, and there were some dramatic swings.
Atlanta took the lead for the first time in the sixth when Ozzie Albies hit an RBI triple thanks to some less-than-stellar fielding from Phillies' center fielder Derek Hill. However, a Ronald Acuña Jr. misplay in the seventh allowed J.T. Realmuto to hit a triple of his own, scoring two runs to put Philly back in front.
Phillies' manager Don Mattingly went for the kill shot by bringing on closer Jhoan Duran in the seventh. He got through that inning fine and came back out for the eighth, facing the heart of Atlanta's order. He got two quick outs before Michael Harris II kept the inning alive with a softly-struck infield single. Duran hit Albies with a pitch after that, bringing Riley to the plate. Duran then left a fastball right in the middle of the zone, and Riley took full advantage, giving Atlanta a lead that Raisel Iglesias held on to in the ninth.
If the Braves win today, then they'll advance to play the two-time defending champion Dodgers in the NLDS. If the Phillies can hold them off behind ace Cristopher Sánchez however, then Game 3 awaits on Thursday.
San Diego Padres 8, Chicago Cubs 0
(San Diego leads 1-0)
Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh inning as the Padres' offense crushed Cubs pitching in the late night game out west.
The Cubs' story this season is that they have an excellent offense and poor pitching, ranking first and last in fWAR respectively. However in Game 1, only one of those things proved true. Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado both hit first inning home runs against Matthew Boyd, getting San Diego off to the perfect start, from which they only added on to their lead.
Meanwhile, the Cubs offense couldn't do much against King. The former Yankee didn't allow a hit until Nico Hoerner singled with one out in the seventh. In total, King shut out Chicago over seven frames, allowing just the one hit and three walks, striking out eight.
In the ninth inning, Padres' pitcher Joe Musgrove returned to the majors after a two-year absence while recovering from Tommy John surgery. He allowed a couple Cubs to reach base, but did end up throwing a scoreless inning.

item.dc:creator: Mike Chiari

item.content:encoded:
Fernando Tatis Jr. Talks Padres' Dominant MLB Playoffs G1 Win vs. Cubs, 'Beautiful Baseball Night'
Fernando Tatís Jr. reflected on what was essentially a perfect night for the San Diego Padres on Tuesday, as they cruised to an 8-0 win over the Chicago Cubs in Game 1 of their National League Wild Card Series.
Speaking to reporters following the one-sided victory, Tatís said, "We couldn't have scripted it any better than what happened tonight. Today was a beautiful baseball night for every San Diegan."
Playing in front of over 47,000 fans at Petco Park in San Diego, the Padres poured it on from the get-go, as they led 2-0 after one inning and 7-0 through five.
Tatís was a big part of the Padres' offensive success in Game 1, as he launched a solo home run to lead off the bottom of the first inning.
All told, Tatís went 2-for-3, walked once, stole a base and scored three runs to go along with the one homer and one RBI.
Veteran third baseman Manny Machado also homered and drove in a pair, while starting pitcher Michael King authored a masterpiece, allowing one hit and no runs, while walking three and striking out eight over seven innings.
King and the San Diego pitching staff notably shut down Cubs outfielder and NL MVP front-runner Pete Crow-Armstrong, as he went 0-for-3 with three strikeouts and one walk.
The Padres are now just one win away from advancing to the National League Division Series for the second time in the past three seasons.
They will send Nick Pivetta to the mound for Wednesday night's Game 2 of the NLWCS, while Chicago will counter with Kevin Gausman.

item.title: [Chicago Tribune] The best advice young Chicago White Sox players received in their 1st postseason
item.dc:creator: LaMond Pope
item.description: HOUSTON — Chicago White Sox pitcher Sean Burke sat next to designated hitter Andrew Benintendi during the flight to Houston ahead of the American League wild-card series. “Kind of just talked about playoffs, his past experiences, some stuff that we need to do,” Burke said on Tuesday afternoon at Daikin Park. “His advice was just kind of keep doing what we’ve been doing the whole year.” That’s the approach the Sox took into the postseason. Several players are experiencing the playoffs for the fir
item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON — Chicago White Sox pitcher Sean Burke sat next to designated hitter Andrew Benintendi during the flight to Houston ahead of the American League wild-card series.
“Kind of just talked about playoffs, his past experiences, some stuff that we need to do,” Burke said on Tuesday afternoon at Daikin Park. “His advice was just kind of keep doing what we’ve been doing the whole year.”
That’s the approach the Sox took into the postseason. Several players are experiencing the playoffs for the first time. That includes Burke, who is in line to pitch in some role in Game 2 against the Houston Astros on Wednesday.
“I don’t think really anything needs to change,” Burke said. “We got here for a reason, and we know we have a good team, we have a talented group. I think just focusing on playing our brand of baseball is going to be good enough for us.”
Benintendi was the only White Sox player in Tuesday’s starting lineup with major-league playoff experience. He played in the postseason in 2016-18 with the Boston Red Sox. The 2018 club won the World Series.
“It’s always nice to make the playoffs,” Benintendi said on Sunday. “I haven’t played in any since 2018. I was with the Yankees, but I was hurt during their run in ’22.
“It’s exciting. It’s always fun. At the least, it’s an experience for everyone in here to dip their toes in it.”
Benintendi is one of the players shortstop Colson Montgomery leaned on.
“If you look at our lineup, it consists of a lot of kind of rookies and guys who this is our first full year,” Montgomery said before Tuesday’s game. “But also, we have a lot of veterans that have been in this scenario. (Outfielders Tommy Pham), (Benintendi), (Randal Grichuk), those guys have definitely been the people we’ve leaned on.
“And they just go out there and they’re telling us, try to make it seem like it’s another game. Go about your routines the exact same because once the game starts, it’s the same thing we’ve been playing 162 games. It can be more magnified. You can make it feel that way, but it’s just kind of the stuff they have been telling us is just take it day by day and just be you.”
Montgomery said it was important not to overanalyze the situation.
“I just feel like when you’re young and you’re hungry and you’re competitive and you’re in a scenario like this, it’s kind of like one of those things where you go out there and play,” he said. “You go out there and you compete. You don’t overanalyze a lot of things. You kind of just go out there and do what you know, and that’s play baseball. We’ve all been playing baseball for our whole lives, so in our eyes this is something that’s not anything different.
“But we’re all excited. All the young guys, we’re all pumped to be here.”
While the team did receive a special letter from Pope Leo XIV, manager Will Venable didn’t feel a special speech was necessary.
“These guys have a full understanding of what this is, even if they haven’t been here before,” Venable said on Tuesday. “We’ve talked about some of the environments and situations that we played in, especially in the second half of this year, going to Wrigley (Field to play the Cubs), going to Yankee Stadium (to play the New York Yankees), whatever it might be, and playing in those high-leverage moments and experiencing that.
“Of course, there’s nothing like the playoffs and, that’s going to be a different beast all in itself and they will have to experience that for themselves. There’s nothing that I can say that can help them feel what it’s going to feel like.”

item.title: [MLB.com] Riley flips Game 1 with 8th-inning blast on 99.9 mph pitch from Phillies' closer
item.dc:creator: Mark Bowman
item.description: ATLANTA -- Austin Riley supported Chris Sale’s strong start, halted the Phillies’ postseason dominance of Atlanta and put six months of frustration behind him with a swing that could make October worth savoring for both him and the Braves. Riley’s three-run homer off All-Star closer Jhoan Duran with two outs in the eighth inning gave the Braves a thrilling 5-3 win over the Phillies in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series on Tuesday afternoon at Truist Park. “I’m happy for Austin Riley,
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- Austin Riley supported Chris Sale’s strong start, halted the Phillies’ postseason dominance of Atlanta and put six months of frustration behind him with a swing that could make October worth savoring for both him and the Braves.
Riley’s three-run homer off All-Star closer Jhoan Duran with two outs in the eighth inning gave the Braves a thrilling 5-3 win over the Phillies in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series on Tuesday afternoon at Truist Park.
“I’m happy for Austin Riley,” Braves manager Walt Weiss said. “It’s been a tough year for him. But this just goes to show you, when the playoffs start, everything starts at zero. Nothing that happened in the regular season really matters. It’s a clean slate. Austin Riley has been a great postseason player.”
Four of Riley’s six career postseason homers have been of the go-ahead variety and three of those have been hit in the eighth inning or later. That eighth inning or later total matches Troy Glaus, Bernie Williams, Jose Altuve and Freddie Freeman for the most in MLB history.
The slugging third baseman previously hit a go-ahead shot in the ninth inning of Game 1 of the NLCS on Oct. 12, 2020, and he hit a go-ahead two-run home run with two outs in the bottom of the eighth in Game 2 of the 2023 NLDS, also against the Phillies. Chipper Jones is the only other Braves player with multiple go-ahead homers in the eighth inning or later of a postseason game.
“I know how my season went,” Riley said. “It’s not the way I wanted it to. But that's the beauty of the postseason. You get a clean slate and go out there and try to do something for the boys and for this city.”
Instead of talking about being on the brink of elimination, the Braves joyfully discussed how everything changed when Riley sent Duran’s 99.9 mph fastball over the right-center-field fence for a go-ahead home run.
Riley doesn’t remember what any of his teammates said after he returned to a jubilant dugout after his home run. Was he also in a haze as he rounded the bases?
“I remember my gum falling out of my mouth,” Riley said.
It was a jaw-dropping moment that put the Braves in an encouraging position.
In the history of the best-of-three Wild Card Series, teams taking a 1-0 lead have gone on to win the series 21 of 24 times (88%), including 17 two-game sweeps. Home teams have won all nine series in which they have gone ahead 1-0, including eight sweeps.
The Phillies had won six of the previous eight postseason games played against the Braves this decade. Philadelphia beat Atlanta in the 2022 and ‘23 NL Division Series.
“It doesn't get more fun than this, playing this game in the postseason,” Weiss said. “You can imagine going from losing the lead to something like that. The swinging emotions are enormous. What a big home run.”
Sale played a significant role in this crucial Game 1 victory. The Braves ace registered nine strikeouts over 6 1/3 innings. Two of the three runs he surrendered came via a J.T. Realmuto triple that Didier Fuentes surrendered with two outs in the seventh.
So where was Sale when the value of his strong effort was preserved by Riley’s home run?
“I was getting some arm care in, and unfortunately the [clubhouse] TV I was watching was on the delay [feed],” he said. “I just heard craziness coming from the entire clubhouse. Everyone's losing their mind, and I'm just sitting there like, ‘Oh, what's going on?’ About four seconds later, you see what happened. I just couldn't be happier for him.”
Coming off two injury-shortened seasons, Riley hit .219 with 19 homers and a .654 OPS during the regular season. Safe to say this was the most frustrating season of the two-time All-Star’s career. This past weekend in Miami, he talked about how relaxing his right shoulder might have helped him hit two homers in last week’s Reds series.
The triple came against a 98.2 mph splitter that was in the middle of the zone. The ball had 109 mph exit velocity and it traveled a Statcast-projected 394 feet.
This home run came against a 99.9 mph four-seamer that was middle in. This is the hardest-thrown pitch Riley has homered against in his career, besting a homer he hit against Jacob deGrom’s 99.7 mph heater on July 1, 2021.
This latest home run had a 104.6 mph exit velocity and it traveled a projected 385 feet.
It would have been a home run in 27 of 30 MLB ballparks. Did Riley know it was gone?
“No, I did not,” he said. “I was just praying as I was running to first.”

item.title: [thebeatdfw.com] Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club
item.dc:creator: Thebeatdfw Staff; Joshua Hemphill
item.description: Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club 24-year-old Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong joined one of the rarest clubs in Major League Baseball this season. The NL MVP favorite became the seventh player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 40+ bases in a single season. item.content:encoded:
Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club
24-year-old Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong joined one of the rarest clubs in Major League Baseball this season. The NL MVP favorite became the seventh player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 40+ bases in a single season.
While there are only a select few talented players who have made the club, there are several players from this generation who have made the cut and also invented clubs of their own.
Here is a list of the 7 players to make the 40/40 club:
RELATED | Top 20 All-Time Greatest Baseball Players
RELATED | MLB Players Who Played In The Little League World Series
1988 Jose Canseco – 42 HR, 40 SB, .307 AVG, .391 OBP, .569 SLG
The founding member of this club, Canseco, predicted he would achieve this milestone. He also drove in a league-leading 124 runs and posted a heavy .569 slugging percentage to coast to a unanimous AL MVP.
Canseco would lose to the Dodgers 4-1 in the World Series, winning the only game with a grand
1996 Barry Bonds – 42 HR, 40 SB, .308 AVG, .461 OBP, .615 SLG
Bonds paired pure athleticism with legendary plate discipline, combining 42 home runs and 40 stolen bases with a career-high 151 walks.
His absurd .461 OBP ensured he was constantly on base to leverage his speed, though his 9.7 WAR effort incredibly finished fifth in a hitter-dominated NL MVP vote that season.
Even with Bonds’ historic run, the Giant’s struggled this season, finishing 68-94 and 4th in the NL West.
1998 Alex Rodriguez – 42 HR, 46 SB, .310 AVG, .360 OBP, .560 SLG
At just 22 years old, A-Rod accomplished what remains the most physically demanding 40/40 season by doing it as a everyday shortstop.
He recorded an MLB-leading 213 hits, which helped him finish the season with a 43.9 Power/Speed number—the highest mark ever achieved in baseball history.
Rodriguez’s Mariners failed to reach the playoffs as well, ending the season at 76-85 and 3rd in the AL West.
2006 Alfonso Soriano – 46 HR, 41 SB, .277 AVG, .351 OBP, .560 SLG
After coming just one home run short with the Yankees in 2002, Soriano left no doubt during his single, explosive season in Washington.
He blasted 46 home runs and swiped 41 bags. Soriano’s season stands out unique because he also hit 41 doubles, creating the game’s only 40/40/40 performance.
The Nationals also failed to reach the postseason, finishing 71-91 and 5th in the NL East.
2023 Ronald Acuna Jr. – 41 HR, 73 SB, .337 AVG, .416 OBP, .596 SLG
Acuña weaponized MLB’s larger bases and rules limiting pitcher disengagements to turn the 40/40 club completely on its head.
While maintaining a career-best .337 batting average, he bashed 41 home runs and ran wild for 73 stolen bases, easily taking home NL MVP honors.
After Acuna’s record-breaking season, the superstar struggled in the postseason, hitting 2-14 and only scoring two runs. The Braves would fall in the NLDS to the Philadelphia Phillies.
2024 Shohei Ohtani – 54 HR, 59 SB, .310 AVG, .390 OBP, .646 SLG
Serving strictly as a designated hitter while rehabbing his throwing arm, Ohtani reached 40/40 in a blistering 126 games—shattering Soriano’s previous speed record of 147 games. He hit a walk-off grand slam to secure the milestone, eventually pushing his totals to 54 home runs and 59 steals to create the 50/50 club.
Ohtani is the only player so far to cap off his historic season winning the World Series, beating the Yankees in 5 games.
2026 Pete Crow-Armstrong – 45 HR, 41 SB, .280 AVG, .372 OBP, .570 SLG
Originally known as a spectacular, defense-first center fielder, PCA shocked the baseball world by developing top-tier power to accompany his elite speed. He tied for the MLB lead with 45 home runs and secured his 40th stolen base during the Cubs’ playoff-clinching victory in late September.
The Chicago Cubs will play in the Wild Card round on Tuesday.
Who do you think had the most impressive season? Let us know!
Pete Crow-Armstrong Joins Elite Company: The 7 Players In The 40/40 Club was originally published on wfnz.com

item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, the San Francisco Giants played their final game of the 2026 regular season.
They lost to the Los Angeles Dodgers (at home) by a score of 5-1.
The Giants also missed the 2026 MLB playoffs.
SF Giants Announce Jung Hoo Lee News
The Giants were without Jung Hoo Lee at the end of the season, as he was placed on the injured list.
Alex Pavlovic of NBC Sports Bay Area wrote (on September 21): “Bryce Eldridge went on the concussion IL. Jung Hoo Lee, the last man standing from Opening Day, is going on the IL with a groin contusion after a poorly placed foul ball yesterday. Mayer and Davidson take their spots. Philip Abner was DFA’d to clear a 40-man spot.”
On Tuesday, the Giants announced injury updates.
Justice delos Santos of Mercury News wrote: “An all-time medical report from the Giants. Just about everyone aside from the Tommy John guys will be ready for spring training.”
The Giants wrote about Lee: “(groin contusion) is fully cleared.”
Lee finished the 2026 regular season batting .276 with 149 hits, 10 home runs, 57 RBIs, 65 runs and 12 stolen bases in 143 games.
Looking At Lee’s Career
Lee has now played three seasons at the MLB level (all with the Giants).
Over 330 career games, the 28-year-old is batting .270 with 336 hits, 20 home runs, 120 RBIs, 153 runs and 24 stolen bases.
ESPN’s Jeff Passan wrote (on December 12, 2023): “Outfielder Jung Hoo Lee’s deal with the San Francisco Giants — six years, $113 million, an opt-out after four seasons — is a monster deal and finally lands the Giants a big-time free agent after missing on Shohei Ohtani, Aaron Judge and others. @JonHeyman was on the news.”
Looking At The Giants
Coming into the year, the Giants had one of the most notable rosters in the National League.
That said, they had a tough season under first-year manager Tony Vitello.
The Giants finished the year as the fourth-place team in the National League West with a 65-97 record.

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the 2026 MLB playoffs, baseball fans. The postseason got started Tuesday with a quartet of Game 1s in the best-of-three Wild Card Series. The Braves came back against the Phillies in the early start, while the White Sox cruised to an easy win against the Astros and . In the late slate, Michael King took a no-hitter into the seventh inning en route to a blowout Padres win over the Cubs.
In these short series, the Game 1 winners are one victory away from the LDS round, and the Game 1 losers are one loss away from their season being over.
The Rays, Guardians, Brewers and Dodgers all secured byes and await the winners in the next round. The Rays are the American League's top seed and will face a division rival in the ALDS, whether it's the Yankees or the Red Sox. The Guardians, despite an 85-77 record that ranks 10th out of the 12 playoff teams, earned the No. 2 seed in the AL and will face either the 84-win White Sox or 81-win Astros in the next round.
The Brewers (103 wins) and Dodgers (100 wins) both hit triple digits in the win column in the regular season, and they will host NLDS Game 1s on Saturday. The Brewers get the Padres-Cubs winner, while the two-time reigning champion Dodgers get either the Braves or the Phillies.
Below is a look at the full 2026 MLB playoff bracket and the playoff schedule.

2026 MLB playoff schedule

item.title: [MLB.com] Red Sox-Yankees AL Wild Card Series Game 1: LIVE on NBC, Peacock
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne; Bryan Hoch
item.description: NEW YORK – One year later, they’re right back at it. The Yankees are preparing to host the Red Sox for another American League Wild Card Series, renewing baseball’s most enduring rivalry in a best-of-three showdown. Tuesday’s Game 1 delivers a rematch of the pairing that took place in the Bronx last October, when Cam Schlittler struck out 12 over eight scoreless innings to quiet the online chirpers and end Boston’s season, propelling his Yankees into the AL Division Series. This time, the prize
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK – One year later, they’re right back at it. The Yankees are preparing to host the Red Sox for another American League Wild Card Series, renewing baseball’s most enduring rivalry in a best-of-three showdown.
Tuesday’s Game 1 delivers a rematch of the pairing that took place in the Bronx last October, when Cam Schlittler struck out 12 over eight scoreless innings to quiet the online chirpers and end Boston’s season, propelling his Yankees into the AL Division Series.
This time, the prize is a trip to Tropicana Field, where the Rays will be waiting to face the winner. These Yankees would gladly sign up for that.
“It's special,” Schlittler said on Monday. “Being able to get that experience last year in Game 3, it's a good feeling to go out there and get the first one.”
You don’t need to flip back to Bucky Dent to find the latest great comeback. These Red Sox seemed to have one foot on the golf course in late June, a managerial change already having taken place as they faced a 15 1/2-game deficit in the division on June 19. They rescued their season, beginning with a four-game sweep of the Yankees at Fenway Park from June 25-28.
“I’ve been watching Red Sox-Yankees since I was a kid. It’s Red Sox-Yankees,” said Tracy. “It’s no secret as far as the rivalry that has existed over the years for a very long time. That’s obvious to everybody. I know there’s always a little extra when those two teams meet. Beyond that, I’m not putting much more into that other than just preparing and getting ready for that series.”
How can I tune in?
Game 1 of the Red Sox-Yankees Wild Card Series is underway at Yankee Stadium. The game will be broadcast on NBC and Peacock.
The Wild Card Series will be available in Spanish on Universo, while Univision Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB Postseason games, beginning with the Wild Card Series.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Tolle has become a fireballing fan favorite in Boston, just as likely to strike someone out on a 98 mph heater as he is to wrap someone into a bear hug. The Red Sox have no reservations about putting the 23-year-old into the hostile territory Yankee Stadium figures to be.
Gray, at 36, is having one of the best seasons of his career in his first year with Boston. He easily leads the Red Sox in quality starts with 20. The Yankees are one of his former teams, and the only one he didn’t perform well for in his career.
Starting pitching is the Yanks’ greatest strength going into this postseason. Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA) built upon his 2025 playoff breakout to establish his place among the league’s most dominant young arms. The Walpole, Mass., product relishes taking on the Sox, for whom he once cheered, and will likely use whatever vitriol he can find on social media as potential rage fuel.
Max Fried (5-5, 2.80 ERA) will follow in Game 2, with Gerrit Cole (10-9, 3.61 ERA) in line for Game 3. Fried has faced Boston twice this year, including eight scoreless innings on April 22 at Fenway Park. He last pitched Sept. 22 vs. the Rays, allowing four runs in 6 2/3 innings. Carlos Rodón (7-3, 2.67 ERA) is likely to be available out of the bullpen as he prepares for a potential ALDS Game 1.
What are the starting lineups?
Red Sox: Schlittler has been a big-time nemesis for the Red Sox, dating back to his coming-out party in the playoffs last year. But Boston did get a jolt from Caleb Durbin in the form of a go-ahead homer over the Green Monster against the Yankees’ ace on June 25, the win that started the 32-5 run by the Red Sox. Recently, Boston hitters have worked overtime on the Trajekt pitching machine, which can mimic any Major League starting pitcher. The Sox have struggled offensively for much of September, particularly with runners in scoring position. But they’ve also lacked multiple key lineup pieces at various parts of the month.
Yankees: Manager Aaron Boone said the Yankees view Tolle as “closer to neutral” in terms of splits, but they also tried to load their lineup with right-handed bats when they faced him in June. They did that again in Game 1, with Anthony Volpe getting the start over Jazz Chisholm Jr. at second base and Amed Rosario inserted at third base.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Red Sox: Aroldis Chapman, a former Yankee, continues to be one of the elite closers in the game at 38 years old. He has one of the league’s best setup men in front of him in righty Garrett Whitlock. In a significant development, the Sox placed their other key high-leverage reliever -- righty Tyron Guerrero, who frequents triple digits with his fastball -- back on the 15-day IL with a right shoulder and lat strain on Sunday’s final day of the regular season. Brayan Bello is the Swiss Army knife of the bullpen, available for bulk relief and also taking down a couple of innings when necessary. The most intriguing roster question for the Red Sox heading into the series was answered Tuesday morning, when Garrett Crochet, who started the season as the ace but hasn’t pitched since April 25, was activated for this series.
Yankees: David Bednar finished his first full season in the Bronx with 35 saves and a 2.50 ERA in 63 appearances, the closer ahead of a relief crew that leaned heavily upon Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick and Tim Hill in the late innings. The Yankees didn’t make a bullpen acquisition at the Trade Deadline, but they added pieces down the stretch by picking up Michael Fulmer and John Schreiber, both of whom could be called upon for valuable outs. Will Warren is also converting into a relief role and could provide length. Ryan Weathers appears to be in play as a potential bullpen piece, adding a big arm to the mix.
Any injuries of note?
Red Sox: Contreras got smoked on the knuckle between his right ring finger and pinkie on Sept. 17, but took two at-bats in the final game of the regular season on Sunday and should be good to go. Guerrero is a big loss in the bullpen for this series. Justin Slaten, a key leverage reliever for Boston the past three seasons, is also out with a right flexor injury.
Masataka Yoshida, one of the few Boston hitters who performed against the Yankees in last year’s postseason series, won’t factor in this year. He’s been out since Aug. 16 with a hamstring strain and likely won’t make it back this season.
Yankees: No story has occupied more space recently than Aaron Judge’s right soleus strain, which typically requires weeks on the injured list. Judge tried to convince the Yankees' brass that he could give it a go for the Wild Card round, but sources confirmed to MLB.com on Tuesday that Judge would would not be on the Wild Card roster vs. Boston. Meanwhile, Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham have both been hitting and running. Weathers is out with a flexor strain but hopes to return.
Who is hot and who is not?
Red Sox: Anthony has understandably had some ups and downs after missing nearly four months with a right hand/wrist injury, but he slashed .333/.375/.633 in his final eight games of the season. From a pitching standpoint, Bello has been a force since he returned from the Minors, posting a 2.11 ERA in 14 appearances, including three starts.
Rutschman has had a hard time getting his bat going since joining the Red Sox at the Aug. 3 Trade Deadline but had a two-hit game in Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader against the Cubs. Abreu is notoriously streaky and he’s been mostly cold in September (.207/.286/.329, one homer, six RBIs). If past history is any indication, he could heat up again in a hurry.
Yankees: Rice hit his team-leading 40th and 41st home runs on Sept. 23 vs. Tampa Bay, claiming a share of the AL lead until Pete Alonso passed him on Friday. Rice, a Cohasset, Mass., product, has belted six homers in September. Bellinger has been productive all month, tying Jones (14) for second on the team in RBIs behind Lombard (16). García enjoyed a productive stretch after arriving in a midseason trade but recently endured a long hitless streak. Ryan McMahon has struggled to produce all year.
Anything else fans might want to know?
This marks the seventh time the rivalry has gone to the postseason stage – all since 1999. Fittingly, the teams have split the first six matchups.
The Yankees had the series edge over Boston this season, winning seven of 13 contests. The Yanks swept three games at Fenway in April and split a pair in June, then were swept in a four-game series in Boston later that month. New York took three of four from the Sox in late August, their most recent meeting.
Though Anthony was a big part of the ‘25 Red Sox team, he missed the postseason with a left oblique strain. He is Boston’s leadoff hitter and could have a big impact on this series. During the World Baseball Classic for Team USA, Anthony displayed the ability to perform on a big stage.

item.title: [MLB.com] Phillies need a Game 2 stopper -- and rock-solid Sánchez is just the guy for the job
item.dc:creator: Paul Casella
item.description: ATLANTA -- While most of the Phillies filtered down the tunnel toward the visitors’ clubhouse following Tuesday afternoon’s stunning loss to the Braves, Cristopher Sánchez lingered briefly in the dugout. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA -- While most of the Phillies filtered down the tunnel toward the visitors’ clubhouse following Tuesday afternoon’s stunning loss to the Braves, Cristopher Sánchez lingered briefly in the dugout.
"I saw him at the end of the game," said Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber, "and it just looked like he was staring out there at the mound. So I think that he knows what he's going to be tasked with for tomorrow."
That task is simple: Keep Philadelphia’s season alive.
It won’t be easy for the Phillies following their 5-3 loss to the Braves in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series at Truist Park. They now need to win back-to-back games to avoid elimination -- something only three of the previous 24 teams to lose Game 1 in a best-of-three Wild Card Series have managed to do (2020 Padres, 2020 Athletics, 2025 Yankees).
If the Phillies have any hopes of becoming the fourth, it all starts on Wednesday afternoon with Sánchez on the hill.
"I just try to be my best self every time I'm out there on the mound and try to go out there and compete every time that I can," Sánchez said via interpreter Diego D'Aniello. "It's a short series, so it's just about going out there and putting as many zeros on the board as I can. On my end, it's about being able to put the team in a good position to win."
Sánchez certainly does that more often than not.
He continued his emergence as one of the game's best pitchers this season by putting together another Cy Young-caliber campaign after finishing as the runner-up last season to Pirates ace Paul Skenes.
As for this year, Sánchez ranked second in the NL in strikeouts (231), second in innings pitched (207) and sixth in ERA (2.91). He did not allow a run for the entire month of May as part of his historic 50 2/3-inning scoreless streak.
But all that matters now is what he does in Game 2.
"Always feel good with Cristopher out there," Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. "The playoffs are momentum-based, it seems like, and really, momentum starts with your starting pitcher."
Now, while the Phillies have the utmost confidence in Sánchez regardless of the mound he's pitching from, it's hard to ignore what he's done pitching on the road compared to pitching within the comforts of Citizens Bank Park.
Sánchez has talked often about how much he loves pitching at home -- and for good reason. He went 12-3 with a 2.23 ERA in 19 home starts this season. He was 6-0 with a 1.94 ERA at home last season.
But on the road?
Sánchez went 6-4 with a 3.87 ERA this season. His career road ERA (3.92) is more than a full run higher than it is at home (2.60).
"It's just about remaining calm and remaining focused when you're about to hit the field," Sánchez said of his Game 2 assignment. "It's about keeping focus on what we do on the field."
Sánchez, of course, also has plenty of familiarity with the Braves.
He's faced them nine times (eight starts) in his career. Four of those starts have come over the past two seasons.
But he has never beaten Atlanta. Sánchez is 0-5 against the Braves -- though that mark may be a bit deceiving. Despite the ugly record, he has a respectable 3.26 ERA in those nine outings, including a 2.19 ERA in four meetings since the start of last season.
That said, some of Atlanta's best hitters have given Sánchez some trouble in the past. Matt Olson, Ozzie Albies, Ronald Acuña Jr. and Austin Riley are a combined 28-for-72 (.389) against the Phillies' co-ace.
But again, none of that matters come Wednesday.
All that matters is what Sánchez does once he takes the mound. The same mound he was so locked in on before departing the ballpark on Tuesday evening.
"Just trying to get a little taste of what it will be like being out there tomorrow," Schwarber said. "Any time he takes the ball for us, we're always excited for that, and we're excited to get out here tomorrow and play a game.
"Let's go. You know what I mean? That's our guy."

item.title: [MLB.com] LIVE: White Sox-Astros AL Wild Card Series Game 1 (Peacock/NBCSN)
item.dc:creator: Brian McTaggart; Scott Merkin
item.description: The Astros, who roared back from an early-season deficit to win their eighth American League West title in 10 seasons Sunday, return to the playoffs following a one-year absence to face the upstart White Sox, who led the AL Central for much of the season before settling for the final Wild Spot in the AL. While this series might not attract the attention of the AL’s other Wild Card Series -- the Yankees and Red Sox -- Astros-White Sox is an intriguing battle featuring a playoff-tested Houston tea
item.content:encoded:
The Astros, who roared back from an early-season deficit to win their eighth American League West title in 10 seasons Sunday, return to the playoffs following a one-year absence to face the upstart White Sox, who led the AL Central for much of the season before settling for the final Wild Spot in the AL.
While this series might not attract the attention of the AL’s other Wild Card Series -- the Yankees and Red Sox -- Astros-White Sox is an intriguing battle featuring a playoff-tested Houston team that has star power in AL Most Valuable Player favorite Yordan Alvarez, former World Series MVP Jeremy Peña and Jose Altuve, one of this generation’s greatest postseason performers, against a Chicago team with some up-and-coming stars.
“I feel like we did the hardest part, which was to get in,” Alvarez said.
The White Sox are led by Miguel Vargas and Munetaka Murakami, one of the best power-hitting duos in baseball. Murakami slammed 35 home runs as a rookie, and Vargas had 33 homers and should receive some downballot MVP votes.
"It feels good,” White Sox designated hitter Andrew Benintendi said. “I think that kind of hit a certain point of the year where you slot yourself in there. Now it’s officially over. The real season starts now."
When is the game and how can I watch it?
Game 1 of the White Sox-Astros Wild Card Series is underway at Daikin Park. The game is being broadcast on Peacock and NBCSN.
The Wild Card Series will be available in Spanish on Universo, while Univision Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB Postseason games, beginning with the Wild Card Series.
Who are the starting pitchers?
White Sox: Hagen Smith, LHP
Key Stats: 1.29 ERA, 28 IP, 13.1 K/9
With a chance to win the American League Central, the White Sox used Sean Burke (11-7, 3.34), Davis Martin (9-8, 3.95) and Anthony Kay (10-9, 4.44) against the last-place Rockies this weekend. Burke is likely lined up for Game 2 behind Game 1 starter Hagen Smith, who got the nod in an expected "bullpen-type game" from manager Will Venable on Monday. Smith is a largely untested rookie, but during his 18 games and 28 innings, he has induced some ugly-looking swings from the opposition.
Astros: AJ Blubaugh, RHP
Key Stats: Led MLB relievers with 96 IP
The 25-year-old rookie will start Tuesday’s Game 1 as the opener of what will be a bullpen game. Blubaugh threw 15 pitches in relief on Friday against the A’s, allowing one run in two-thirds of an inning.
Blubaugh led the Major Leagues with 27 relief appearances of at least two innings this season, the most by an Astros pitcher since Dave Veres had 27 in 1995. Blubaugh led all relievers with a career-high 96 innings. He has thrown more than two innings in only five games this season.
Blubaugh faced the White Sox three times in the regular season, allowing no runs, four hits and two walks while striking out three in four innings.
What are the starting lineups?
White Sox: With the Astros going with a bullpen game, the White Sox are trotting out this lineup.
Astros: The last three spots in the order are occupied by outfielders. Rookie Lucas Spence, who hit four homers in the season’s final series, earned the start in center, and Cam Smith will be in right field, hitting eighth.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
White Sox: Venable is not set on one lockdown closer, although Grant Taylor is coming off a dominant campaign with a 2.25 ERA and 106 strikeouts in 84 innings. So, Taylor could be used for two innings in the sixth and seventh, or try to finish off a victory in the ninth. The same holds true for relievers such as Sean Newcomb, Bryan Hudson and the rookie additions of Smith and Noah Schultz.
Astros: A seven-inning outing by starter Hayden Wesneski on Saturday and Sunday’s blowout win in the regular-season finale have Houston’s bullpen in really good shape heading into the postseason, especially with the Astros contemplating a bullpen game for Tuesday. They could get multiple innings out of the bullpen from Josh Hendrickson, Miguel Ullola and AJ Blubaugh in an effort to get the ball to setup man Bryan Abreu and closer Josh Hader, who finished the season with a 1.01 ERA and 26-for-26 in save chances. He hasn’t pitched since Wednesday.
Any injuries of note?
White Sox: Chase Meidroth has been dealing with left hamstring discomfort, among myriad nagging injuries. He sat out most of the weekend against the Rockies after leaving early from Thursday’s playoff-clincher in Kansas City, but should be available Tuesday.
Astros: Isaac Paredes fouled a ball off his knee Saturday in West Sacramento and was in the lineup for Sunday’s season finale, but the Astros were so concerned about the knee that they called up infielder Raynel Delgado to give them some coverage at third base. Center fielders Daulton Varsho (wrist) and Brice Matthews (knee) both landed on the IL last week, so neither will be available for the Wild Card Series.
Who is hot and who is not?
White Sox: Colson Montgomery was a deserving All-Star candidate who was passed over, but has found rough going since the break. In fact, Montgomery finished the season with a .197 average and set the single-season Major League record with 227 strikeouts. He spoke eloquently pregame Sunday about being focused on doing anything to help the team and looking for a reset starting with the playoffs.
Miguel Vargas’ season has been a revelation overall, with 33 homers, 31 doubles, 22 stolen bases, 101 walks, 93 RBIs and 106 runs scored. Munetaka Murakami also seems back on track, with his 35 homers tying Ron Kittle for the second-highest single-season home run total for a White Sox rookie trailing only Jose Abreu (36 in 2014).
Astros: Yordan Alvarez won the AL batting title and will likely add his first AL Most Valuable Player to his resume following a season in which he slashed .316/.432/.601 with 105 runs, 34 doubles, 42 homers, 106 RBIs and 109 walks. Jeremy Peña slashed .353/.358/.706 with five homers and nine RBIs in the Astros’ final 12 games.
Christian Walker had a 1.167 OPS with four homers in the last eight games, Yainer Diaz slashed .350/.377/.581 with six homers and 17 RBIs in 34 games since Aug. 16 and rookie Lucas Spence was 6-for-15 with four homers, a triple and nine RBIs in the final four games of the season.
Taylor Trammell finished the season 0-for-20.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• The Astros have lost seven consecutive home playoff games, dating to 2023.
• This is the third time the Astros and White Sox have met in the playoffs. The White Sox swept Houston in the 2005 World Series, and the Astros eliminated the White Sox in four games in the 2021 ALDS.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox will be taking on the New York Yankees in the American League wild-card round this year, which is a rematch from last season.
Boston was able to clinch a spot in the postseason following an impressive run during the middle of the year to get back into the race. But the Red Sox couldn’t do enough to overtake the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East, and now they will be entering a three-game series that will determine their fate.
The longtime rivals are gearing up for Game 1 of the highly anticipated series, with each trying to make a statement against the other. New York won the season series 7-6, but the entire matchup was extremely close, leading to the thought that this playoff matchup will be as well.
Last season, the Yankees defeated the Red Sox in three games to move on to the ALDS. Boston will be looking for some revenge here, and the series is again being played in New York.
Jarren Duran Decision Made by Red Sox
Ahead of Game 1, the Red Sox have now released the lineup that they will use against the Yankees. Within the lineup, outfielder Jarren Duran will be hitting seventh for Boston today.
Duran will be playing in left field.
Red Sox 9/29
R. Anthony DH
A. Rutschman C
W. Contreras 1B
W. Abreu RF
C. Rafaela CF
N. Sogard 2B
J. Duran LF
T. Story SS
C. Durbin 3B
P. Tolle SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 29, 2026
Duran has seen a tough season at the plate take place, and it’s hurt the overall ceiling of this Red Sox team. Overall, the former All-Star has hit .207 with 20 home runs, 69 RBIs, and 21 stolen bases, while posting an OPS of .627.
Boston has been waiting for Duran to break out of his slump all season long, but to this point, nothing has worked. But if he can get his bat going in the playoffs, his struggles from the regular season will be forgiven.
Can Red Sox Take Down Yankees?
For the Red Sox to win this series, guys like Duran are going to need to step up heavily. New York will be without star Aaron Judge due to injury, and the Red Sox need to take advantage of this fact.
Boston’s pitching staff will be counted on heavily in this series as they try to match the strong starting rotation from the Yankees. But luckily for the Red Sox, the team will be getting back ace left-hander Garrett Crochet from injury.
It has been a long time coming for Crochet, with him last pitching on April 25 for this team. Crochet has been trying to come back all year, but the Red Sox finally saw progress over the last few weeks, and he has been added to the playoff roster.
If Crochet can make an impact as a relief pitcher, it could go a long way for this team against the Yankees. Boston is behind the eight ball when it comes to the pitching in the series, and Crochet gives them at least a fighting chance.
The Red Sox and Yankees will kick off the opening game of the series at 5:00 p.m. PT/8:00 p.m. ET from Yankee Stadium.

item.content:encoded:
The Major League Baseball playoffs begin on Tuesday, September 29, and kicking things off in the National League Wild Card round is a premier matchup between the Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves.
It's a marquee matchup between two bigger NL East rivals, and because we are just a few hours away from first pitch, both team's have revealed their 26-man rosters for the series and dropped their game one lineup for the Tuesday matinee.
For the Braves, Ha-Seong Kim is IN the starting lineup for the series opener.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Quietly Cut Ties with 27-Year-Old Player Before Phillies Playoff Series
Ha-Seong Kim Batting 9th; Playing SS for Phillies Series Opener
Here is the full Atlanta Braves batting order for 9/29, per @UnderdogMLB:
"Braves 9/29: D. Baldwin C R. Acuña Jr. RF M. Olson 1B M. Dubón LF M. Harris II CF O. Albies 2B A. Riley 3B M. Yastrzemski DH H. Kim SS C. Sale SP"
As you can see, Ha-Seong Kim is in the lineup batting ninth and playing shortstop.
Other lineup notes include Austin Riley batting seventh and Mike Yastrzemski getting the nod as the DH. Drake Baldwin bats leadoff and forms a battery with Chris Sale, and Mauricio Dubon is out in left field, serving as the cleanup hitter.

item.title: [MLB.com] Red Sox-Yankees position-by-position breakdown
item.dc:creator: Anthony Castrovince

item.content:encoded:
Apple vs. Microsoft. Coke vs. Pepsi. Marvel vs. DC. Ford vs. General Motors.
All child’s play compared to Yankees vs. Red Sox.
Though seeded as Wild Cards, New York and Boston are heavyweight entries in the 2026 postseason field. And only one can advance out of the best-of-three Wild Card Series that begins -- and takes place entirely -- in the Bronx on Tuesday.
The Yankees have survived most of the season without captain Aaron Judge, while the Red Sox survived a brutal start that had them 14 games under .500 in late June.
But who will survive this short and scintillating series at Yankee Stadium? Let’s break it down, position by position, and we are sure to find the unmistakably correct prediction, right? Right?!
Catcher
Austin Wells just hasn’t produced with the consistency he did in his Rookie of the Year finalist season in 2024 or the power he had in last year’s 20-homer, 20-double campaign. He’s a fantastic framer and blocker, and that could matter more in the postseason than his bat given the pitching staff’s increased importance in a short series. But Rutschman has those same strengths, along with an elite caught stealing track record, to go with higher offensive upside in a season in which he’s posted an above-average OPS+.
Edge: Red Sox
First base
The Red Sox have a major asset, but also a major question mark in Willson Contreras. He was a monumental offseason pickup in a trade with the Cardinals. The veteran produced his best offensive season yet, with an OPS over .900 and career-highs in homers and RBIs.
But when Contreras was plunked in the hand by a pitch late in the regular season, it complicated the equation. As of this writing, it was still not clear if he would suit up for the Wild Card Series. Even if he does, he might need some time to get back in the swing of things, given the impact hand discomfort can have on a power stroke.
So the Yankees’ successful midseason acquisition of Luis García Jr. looms large here. After an offensive breakthrough with the Nationals, he’s remained an above-average producer in pinstripes, finishing off his 30-homer season. And the Yanks have a dangerous platoon option in Paul Goldschmidt, the consummate pro who still does big damage to lefties – no small tool in their chest given the lefty leaning complexion of the Red Sox’s starting staff.
Edge: Yankees
Second base
Between the trade of the disappointing Marcelo Mayer and a late-season injury to Anthony Siegler, the Red Sox are left piecing things together here with Nick Sogard and veteran Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Sogard’s contact skills can play up in the postseason even if he doesn’t produce much power.
But the Yankees have higher upside here. Though Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s walk year saw statistical regression, he ultimately provided league-average offense with north of 40 steals. He could augment his open-market asking price with a strong showing.
Edge: Yankees
Shortstop
Trevor Story was sidelined for the Sox for about three months with a sports hernia that required surgery. He showed signs of offensive life in September, but this will nevertheless go down as one of his worst seasons at the plate in limited time.
The Yankees look like they have a star in the making in George Lombard Jr. While no one knows how the fresh-faced 21-year-old, who only debuted on Aug. 4, will perform under the bright lights of the postseason, he’s already had some huge hits for the Yanks and his plate discipline, high baseball IQ, fluid actions and plus speed all make him dangerous in a short series.
Edge: Yankees
Third base
The hot corner has been cold to the Yankees this year. Veteran Ryan McMahon’s first full season in the Bronx has been a drastic disappointment and his right-handed-hitting complement Amed Rosario hasn’t been much better. The Yankees were toying with the idea of working former shortstop Anthony Volpe here.
As for Boston, while replacing free-agent departure Alex Bregman was a tall order, a trade for Caleb Durbin, a reigning NL Rookie of the Year finalist with the Brewers, has paid enormous dividends. Durbin looked lost in the headlights for his first couple months in a major market, but his midseason ignition matched that of the club at large. He has great range at third, is among the more difficult batters in MLB to strike out and logged 25 doubles for the second straight season.
Edge: Red Sox
Left field
After getting spurned by Juan Soto in free agency the previous winter, the Yankees did not let Cody Bellinger get away. In his second season with the Yanks, the former NL MVP became an All-Star Game MVP in the midst of providing his usual disciplined, contact-and-power profile at the plate and elite defense in the grass. He’s been on this postseason stage plenty of times before.
There was hope in Boston that Roman Anthony would break out into superstardom this season. But a significant finger ligament injury early in the season got in the way, opening the door for Jarren Duran to see the bulk of time in left while producing an OPS+ more than 20% below league average. Anthony returned in late August, and it should shock no one if this postseason turns into his coming-out party. But for now, we’ve got to go with the more accomplished veteran here.
Edge: Yankees
Center field
The Sox had another late-season health scare with Ceddanne Rafaela, their rangy, speedy power-armed gem in center field. Rafaela was finishing up his finest offensive season to date when he suffered a right quad strain a few weeks back. But a clean MRI in the season’s final week allowed him to return.
Meanwhile, Trent Grisham’s September hamstring strain gave the Yankees their own center-field concern. Grisham’s absence allowed 25-year-old rookie Spencer Jones to showcase his excellent raw power and athleticism. Grisham could be back for this series. But Rafaela’s offensive breakthrough and Gold Glove defense carry the way here.
Edge: Red Sox
Right field
Judge’s calf injury is probably the biggest X-factor in the entire postseason field. The Yankees were cagey about its severity, and manager Aaron Boone said the club was preparing for a Wild Card Series without the captain. Judge was intent on trying to make his way back. But ultimately, Judge was left off the Bombers' Wild Card roster, so they'll be down one of the best hitters on the planet.
For the Red Sox, Wilyer Abreu is ready for his close-up. He was a durable doubles machine who also reached career highs in homers and RBIs, he dramatically improved his production against left-handed pitching, and he has range and a mammoth arm in right. His surge was essential in the Sox returning to the postseason.
Edge: Red Sox
Designated hitter
With Masataka Yoshida out with a hamstring strain, Boston will utilize a DH platoon that includes Roman Anthony against righties and Jahmai Jones against lefties.
In a season that has included so little Judge, the Yankees have gotten a ton out of Ben Rice. Last season’s surprise ascendence for the New England native has proven to be only an appetizer. Rice showed he can mash both lefties and righties alike in clearing the 40-homer threshold, getting selected as a first-time All-Star and earning down-ballot MVP support.
Edge: Yankees
Starting pitching
Cam Schlittler’s likely Cy Young-winning breakthrough in 2026 came on the heels of him carving up the Red Sox club he grew up rooting for in last year’s Wild Card Series. He pairs with Max Fried and Gerrit Cole to give the Yankees a terrifying top end of the rotation in this short series, even if the finish on Cole’s pitches is not yet what it was prior to Tommy John.
While the Yankees deserve the edge here, that’s not to suggest the Sox are slouches in the starting department. That they got to this point essentially without Garrett Crochet took a lot of fortitude, and Payton Tolle’s fantastic rookie campaign was one of the most fun storylines of the season. Sonny Gray remains an absolute command artist in his age-36 season, and Ranger Suarez was a terrific offseason signing who drastically limits the kind of hard contact that can change games in October.
Still, it’s the Yanks here.
Edge: Yankees
Bullpen
These are two top-five relief units in terms of both ERA and expected ERA. Both are excellent at suppressing long balls, which is crucial in October.
The Yankees have a strong ninth-inning anchor in David Bednar, whose elite ability to generate chase with his four-steam/split/curve mix can neutralize even the biggest bats. Paul Blackburn has gone from oft-injured starter to absolute force of nature in the setup role, and Brent Headrick has also undergone a massive transformation as a member of the Yankees ‘pen, for whom he has emerged as a whiff machine. The strength of the starting staff has trickled down to a Yankees bullpen that ranks among the lowest innings workloads of any relief unit in MLB this season.
With Tyron Guerrero’s recent return from injury and the presence of Garrett Whitlock, Greg Weissert and lefty Jovani Morán, the Sox are well-situated in their bridge to the ninth. And in the ninth, they’ve got the ageless Aroldis Chapman, whose age-38 season has seen him produce yet another sub-2.00 ERA, another ERA+ more than 100% better than league average and upper-echelon velo and strikeout rates. He recently returned from a late-season lat issue. Between Chapman’s presence and the possibility that Crochet’s elite arsenal impacts the ‘pen in his potential return from injury, the Red Sox earn the edge.
Edge: Red Sox
Prediction
The Yankees were the better team in record and run differential, and they did it mostly without Judge. They hold the home-field and rotation advantages, have a higher run-scoring baseline and are, therefore, the clear favorites.
All reasons why I’m taking the Red Sox in three. Because baseball.

item.content:encoded:
The MLB playoffs begin today!! (September, 29.) The action begins with the National League Wild Card matchup between the Atlanta Braves and the Philadelphia Phillies.
First pitch is at 2:15 p.m. EST, and both teams are deploying very formidable starters. For Atlanta, it is rolling with Chris Sale in the series opener, and the Phillies are opting to go with Jesus Luzardo as their starter.
Both teams have officially announced their lineup, and for the Braves, the lineup drop features a notable Austin Riley decision.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Suddenly Add 6-Year MLB Veteran Before Phillies WC Series
Braves' Austin Riley Batting 7th in Series Opener
In the NLWC series opener against the Phillies, Austin Riley will bat seventh and play third base, which isn't a huge surprise.
Here is the full Atlanta Braves batting order, per @UnderdogMLB:
"Braves 9/29 D. Baldwin C R. Acuña Jr. RF M. Olson 1B M. Dubón LF M. Harris II CF O. Albies 2B A. Riley 3B M. Yastrzemski DH H. Kim SS C. Sale SP"
A few lineup notes: Mike Yastrzemski gets the start at DH, with the anticipation that Luzardo won't throw very long, and Ha-Seong Kim gets the start at SS. Mauricio Dubon is the team's cleanup hitter, and Ozzie Albies (who crushes lefties) will bat sixth.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Quietly Cut Ties with 27-Year-Old Player Before Phillies Playoff Series
Looking at Austin Riley's 2026 Season
Now that the regular season is officially in the books, we can take a look at Austin Riley's season as a whole.
Over 159 games played and 566 total at-bats, Austin Riley batted .219 with 19 home runs and a career-low OPS+ of 80.
He also added 21 doubles, 72 RBI, 64 runs scored, and 124 hits to the Braves' regular-season offense.
However, the regular season is in the past, and Austin Riley can write all those wrongs by having a big moment or two in the MLB playoffs. Riley would likely be the first to admit he had a poor offensive season, but October baseball can bring a breath of fresh air to players who struggled over the past several months.

item.content:encoded:
The Houston Astros enter the postseason with the AL MVP favorite in their lineup.
Yordan Alvarez should be considered the most feared hitter in baseball for this year's playoffs.
But the rest of Houston's lineup has been mediocre at best.
"The Astros have the presumptive AL MVP in Yordan Alvarez, but the rest of the offense has produced a .233/.300/.396 line this year," Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter wrote. "He will need to replicate his memorable performance in the 2023 ALCS for pretty much the entirety of October."
Clearly, the Astros rely on Alvarez to do most of their offensive damage, but he may not be the AL West club's "X-Factor" during the Wild Card Series against the Chicago White Sox.
Instead, Reuter has tabbed rookie center fielder Lucas Spence as someone who can help Houston make a deep postseason run.
"Lucas Spence went 6-for-18 with four home runs in five games after being recalled from Triple-A when [Daulton] Varsho and [Brice] Matthews were placed on the injured list," Reuter added. "He suddenly looks like the no-doubt starting center fielder for the club's playoff run."
MORE: Pirates urged to re-sign Brandon Lowe if they ‘want to be taken seriously’
Varsho is unavailable in the Wild Card Series due to left wrist inflammation caused by cysts.
He is a Gold Glove outfielder but has hit poorly following a midseason trade from the Toronto Blue Jays.
Spence has just 19 MLB games under his belt but looks up for the challenge, hitting the first three home runs of his career in a single game during the last week of the regular season against the Athletics.

item.title: [themorningsun.com] What went wrong? Tigers boss dissects a disappointing 2026 season
item.dc:creator: Tribune News Service
